espn-604005.headline: Wales opened the door. England have been through it before
beats: England beat New Zealand 33–19 at home on 15 November 2025. Win again and it is a second successive win over New Zealand for the first time in 23 years.

New Zealand lost 35–28 to Wales last weekend, after Wales stared down the haka. Maro Itoje has called a squad meeting to settle England's own response. England have won four straight, the last 78–15 over Japan with 13 tries.

Steve Borthwick has made nine changes to go full-strength, with George Furbank, Seb Atkinson and Ollie Chessum back from injury. Win by 16 or more and England go third in the world, with New Zealand down to fifth below them.
New Zealand's next Test after this is Chile at home next October, which is a long time to sit on either result.

espn-604006.headline: Scotland's third captain in a week, Wales level on 15
beats: A shoulder injury has ruled out Rory Darge, so Stafford McDowall leads Scotland, their third captain in a week. Gregor Townsend has made 11 changes anyway, with Tom Jordan at 10, Ollie Smith at full-back and only Zander Fagerson kept among the forwards.
The rotation comes with something riding on it. Scotland and Wales are level on 15 points in the North. Fourth plays the 7th-place final, and fifth plays the 9th.

Japan conceded 78 at Twickenham last week, and Eddie Jones has changed nine, including the whole front row. Their 21–28 loss in Wales the week before is the kinder guide. A Scotland win moves nobody in the rankings.
Fin Russell and Blair Kinghorn rest after a 15–12 win over Australia that produced two tries. Four would bring a bonus point, the tidier way to stay ahead of Wales.

espn-604007.headline: Erasmus barred, and the France referee has the whistle
beats: Rassie Erasmus is barred from the Aviva Stadium, serving a six-match ban that came out of the 21–19 defeat in Paris on 13 November. World Rugby has handed this game to Christophe Ridley, the referee involved in that controversy.

Ireland have scored 13 tries in two home wins this month, 42–12 against Argentina and 43–15 against Fiji. They scored 13 points the last time South Africa came, losing 24–13 on this ground on 22 November 2025.

Dan Sheehan leads them from No. 8 on his 50th cap. Andy Farrell declined to comment on the ban. South Africa lost Ruan Nortje to a training niggle, and Franco Mostert starts at lock beside Eben Etzebeth.
Any Ireland win takes South Africa off the top of the world rankings, with New Zealand going above them. The ban runs six matches. The ranking can go in one.

espn-604008.headline: Miotti turned down Argentina to start against Fiji
beats: Domingo Miotti won 10 caps for Argentina, the last in July 2022, and turned down a recall from Felipe Contepomi in July 2026 to keep his Italian eligibility. At 30, the Montpellier fly-half makes his Italy debut at No. 10 in Udine, in place of Paolo Garbisi.

His first Test for Italy comes a week after Italy lost 19–14 to Argentina in Genoa, the closest of their six straight defeats. Injuries on the wings sent Ange Capuozzo out there and Tommy Allan to full-back, which is how the shirt came free.
Fiji have conceded 54 to France and 43 to Ireland in a fortnight, and Jake White has kept the same backline for Udine. Win and Italy go above Fiji into 10th in the world.
Gonzalo Quesada expects a tight game. That is the kind a new fly-half is picked to close out.

espn-604009.headline: France need four tries and a fly-half kept in one piece
beats: Matthieu Jalibert starts at 10 for the first time since 20 September, after a quadriceps injury and a relapse in mid-October. Thomas Ramos and Romain Ntamack are both injured, so last week Maxime Lucu, a scrum-half by trade, ran the show in the 21–19 win over South Africa.

A bonus-point win guarantees France top spot in the North and a place in the final on 29 November. Fabien Galthié also wants Jalibert whole for that final, and Planet Rugby would be surprised to see him play past 40 minutes.

Argentina conceded 42 to Ireland, then won 19–14 in Italy. Julián Montoya returns as captain in seven changes. Their last win over France was 33–25 in Buenos Aires in 2024, and even a draw at the Stade de France would lift them to seventh in the world, above Australia.
France need four tries. Their fly-half may be on the field for only half of them.

espn-604010.headline: Wales beat the side that put 93 on Australia
beats: Wales scored five tries past New Zealand in Cardiff on 14 November and won 35–28. In October, New Zealand beat Australia 50–19 and 43–21.

Australia have lost four straight, the latest 12–15 to Scotland at Murrayfield. Les Kiss has changed five of his pack and benched Fraser McReight, the current John Eales Medalist, for Carlo Tizzano. The backline that lost in Edinburgh stays as it was.

Steve Tandy has gone back to the XV that beat Japan. Aaron Wainwright is fit again after missing the New Zealand win, and Josh Adams is back after being rested. Win by 16 or more and Wales go above Australia into eighth in the world.
Australia's last win, in September, was 42–38 over South Africa. South Africa beat Wales 43–0 in July. Form is less transitive than it looks.
